title: Electric Current and Circuits
seo_title: Grade 9 Science: Electric Current and Circuits Worksheets (MATATAG)

standard_text: Electric current, voltage and resistance; Ohm's law; series and parallel circuits; electrical energy and efficiency. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 9, Quarter 1: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 9 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 1: Force, Motion, and Energy): ohm's law, series circuits, parallel circuits, efficiency and energy transformations and sources of electrical energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Efficiency = useful energy out ÷ energy in × 100%.
body_html:
How to think about it

For many conductors, V = IR: doubling the potential difference doubles the current. In a series circuit the current is the same everywhere, the voltages add up to the source voltage, and R(total) = R₁ + R₂. In a parallel circuit every branch has the full voltage, the branch currents add up, and adding a branch lowers the total resistance.

Devices transform electrical energy into other forms, but some always becomes waste heat. Efficiency = useful output ÷ input × 100%. Electricity in the Philippines comes from coal, natural gas, geothermal, hydro, solar and wind plants; each source has benefits and costs.

Example

A 9.0 V battery and a 30 Ω resistor. Current?

I = V ÷ R = 9.0 ÷ 30

Answer: 0.30 A

Example

A lamp uses 60 J and gives 6 J of light. Efficiency?

6 ÷ 60 × 100%

Answer: 10%

Common mistakes

  • Thinking current is used up along a series circuit.
  • Adding parallel resistances to get the total resistance.
  • Calling hydroelectric power energy-free: it still changes rivers and habitats.

What does the I–V graph for a fixed resistor (at constant temperature) look like?
c: A horizontal line: no current ever flows.
A straight line through the origin: current is directly proportional to potential difference.
A curve: resistance increases as the filament gets hotter.
Current flows in one direction only: resistance is very high in reverse.

items.q: Is crude oil a renewable or a non-renewable energy source?
c: neither, because it is not a source of energy
